root_causes.description: The payment service is the direct downstream dependency of checkout and is failing to complete gRPC/HTTP calls (request-abort injection), causing checkout callers to hang until the 10s client timeout is exhausted. Server-side payment span error rate stays flat because the abort terminates the request before a normal status is recorded, while the caller observes a hard timeout.

evidence.observed_value: checkout → cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog (payment is a direct synchronous dependency of checkout)
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout calls to payment complete promptly and payment spans record normal status

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99=10000.0 ms, p50=10000.0 ms, p95=10000.0 ms (latency pinned at the 10s timeout ceiling) at 07:51:35–07:58:35
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout server p99 < 100 ms (cart p99=4.83 ms, shipping p99=9.79 ms in same window)

evidence.observed_value: payment server error_rate=0.000 across window (aborted calls never surface as STATUS_CODE_ERROR on the callee)

root_causes.description: Checkout exhibits the dominant observable anomaly: server p99 latency is pinned at the 10,000 ms ceiling with no accompanying error-rate increase, indicating checkout is blocking on a slow/aborted downstream call rather than failing fast.

evidence.observed_value: checkout CPU usage ~0.002 cores (no resource exhaustion)
evidence.expected_baseline: steady-state checkout CPU usage of a few millicores

root_causes.description: Frontend inherits elevated end-to-end latency because it synchronously calls checkout; its p99 also saturates the 10s ceiling, consistent with a downstream propagation rather than an independent frontend fault.

evidence.observed_value: product-catalog mean=4014.0 ms, p95=10000 ms, p99=10000 ms

remediation_steps: Inspect payment deployment/config for the injected http.abort fault (e.g., flagd flag 'paymentFailure'/'http.abort') and disable or flip the flag to restore normal responses.
Verify payment pod health and restart the payment pods if the abort injection is a runtime fault handler stuck in a bad state.
Add/verify a bounded client timeout and circuit breaker on checkout calls to payment so a hung dependency fails fast instead of pinning checkout p99 at 10s.
Confirm recovery by re-querying checkout p99 latency and payment error/request rates across a 5-minute window; p99 should return below 100 ms.
